candidate.answerReason: Translating both endpoints by the same vector leaves their difference unchanged, so placement does not affect the vector's coordinates.

methods.label: Translation cancellation
methods.explanation: If the endpoints are \(A\) and \(B\), the vector is \(B-A\). Translating both endpoints by the same vector \(t\) gives \((B+t)-(A+t)=B-A\). Thus a fixed free vector has the same coordinates wherever it is placed. In fixed axes, its coordinates depend on both magnitude and direction. A is correct.
methods.levelReason: Endpoint differences and coordinate translation are within the required plane-vector scope.
